messages.author: 29ae35da1a53a211
messages.subject: Fitting a basic 2-state HMM
parts:
Hi, 

I'm just getting started out with NIMBLE and am trying to get a 2-state HMM (with gamma state-dependent densities) up and running. I would like to eventually fit a more complex model using MCEM. 

So far, I can not get the nimbleModel to run without errors. Right now, I am seeing the following error: 

> Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits, check = FALSE, dimensions=list(T=c(2,2)))
defining model...
Detected phi as data within 'constants'.
Error in genVarInfo3() : 
  There is a problem with some indexing in this line: p <- T[theta[i_minus_1], 1:2].
One way this can happen is if you wanted to provide a vector of indices but did not include it in constants.

And here's all of the code I am running (or rather attempting to run): 

## define HMM
code <- nimbleCode({

  a[1] ~ dnorm(-2, 1) 
  gam[1] <- exp(a[1])/(1+exp(a[1]))
  a[2] ~ dnorm(-2, 1) 
  gam[2] <- exp(a[2])/(1+exp(a[2]))

  T[1,1] <- 1-gam[1]
  T[2,1] <- gam[2]
  T[1,2] <- gam[1]
  T[2,2] <- 1-gam[2]
    
  phi <- c(.5, .5)
  theta[1] ~ dcat(prob = phi)
  
  for(i in 2:k) {
    p <- T[theta[i-1],]
    theta[i] ~ dcat(prob = p)
  }
  
  for (i in 1:k) {
    y[i] ~ dgamma(shape=alp[theta[i]], rate=bet[theta[i]])
  }
  
  for(i in 1:2){
    alp[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
    bet[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
  }
  
})


y <- rgamma(100, 1, 1)
k <- 100

alp <- numeric(2)
bet <- numeric(2)

## define model constants, data, and initial values
constants <- list(k=k, phi=c(1/2,1/2))
data <- list(y = y)
inits <- list(theta=sample(x=c(1,2), size = 100, replace = T), a = rep(-2,2), 
              alp=c(1,1), bet=c(1,1))

## create model object
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits, check = FALSE, dimensions=list(T=c(2,2)))


If anyone could point me in the right direction, it'd be much appreciated! I have also tried to go through the R code from the Efficient MCMC Sampling for HHMMs paper but am not familiar with most of the models used in capture-recapture. 

Thank you, 

Vianey

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Fitting a basic 2-state HMM
parts:
Hi Vianey,

NIMBLE can not yet handle stochastic indices.  You have theta[i] as the index to alp, and theta[i] ~ dcat(p), so theta[i] is a stochastic index.

Perry

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Fitting a basic 2-state HMM
parts:
Vianey, this approach I'm going to suggest is not the most computationally efficient, but it does work.

Until we implement stochastic indexing (e.g., being able to index alp[] using the stochastic index theta[i], you can side-step the issue using:
for (i in 1:k) {

shape_param[i] <- equals(theta[i],1)*alp[1] + equals(theta[i],2)*alp[2]
    rate_param[i]  <- equals(theta[i],1)*bet[1] + equals(theta[i],2)*bet[2]
    y[i] ~ dgamma(shape=shape_param[i], rate=rate_param[i])
}


Daniel

NIMBLE can not yet handle stochastic indices.  You have theta[i] as the index to alp, and theta[i] ~ dcat(p), so theta[i] is a stochastic index.
